significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that LLMs can use a self-constructed discrete notation that "match[es] natural-language CoT accuracy while using substantially fewer tokens," with symbol corruption causally reducing performance and cross-model transfer indicating partly shared structure; this is principally a form-(ii) causal claim supplemented by measurable efficiency and transfer relations, not a general law of intelligence. It would establish both a substantive phenomenon—accurate, compressed reasoning outside ordinary grammar—and a functional mechanism—that the dialect symbols carry task-relevant information—constraining choices between verbal, discrete-symbolic, and continuous reasoning substrates studied in work such as COCONUT, but it would not prove independence from natural-language priors because the models and legends remain grounded in natural-language pretraining. True and false outcomes are distinguishable, although the negative branch would only rule out useful dialect induction in the asserted task/model scope rather than show that natural language is necessary. Topic-substitution check: merely restating "the relationship between language and AI intelligence" would not support this score; the extra value comes from the specific accuracy–compression, corruption, and transfer claims, placing it somewhat above the topic's obvious comparison but below a decisive language–intelligence law.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the "legend mapping recurrent reasoning moves to short invented symbols," together with the proposed compact dialect as a decode-time intervention; it is ex ante because it can be selected before solving and used to reduce reasoning tokens rather than merely explain an observed failure afterward. The hypothesis asserts applicability across "problems/models" and partial cross-model transfer, so after re-extraction it predicts useful compression, corruption sensitivity, and some shared structure, although the exact legend may still need reinvention and no quantitative transfer law is asserted. Downstream uptake could include model builders or deployment practitioners choosing efficient, inspectable reasoning formats, not only researchers analyzing language–thought coupling, satisfying the lead-time and non-researcher-uptake tie-breaks. Topic-substitution check: the broad topic alone supplies neither this legend nor an actionable inference-time dialect, so the reach score rests on claim-specific handles rather than the importance of language research.
